ai.description: Gerrhopilus thurstoni is a slender, worm-like snake reaching 20 cm. It is uniform dark brown with a paler snout and tail tip. Key features include 18–20 midbody scale rows and a rounded head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gerrhopilus thurstoni* is best distinguished by its distinctively dark, uniform purplish-brown coloration, which lacks the pale, unpigmented snout tip seen in similar species.
ai.habitat: Thurston's worm snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Thurston's worm snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours burrowing through leaf litter and loose soil in search of small invertebrates like termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gerrhopilus thurstoni* is oviparous, laying small clutches of elongated eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: Gerrhopilus thurstoni is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at mid-to-high elevations.
